title: An LLM-assisted Pipeline for Identifying ClinicalTrials.gov Registry Changes and Their Association with Primary Endpoint Positivity
desc: Registration of randomized clinical trials (RCTs) in a public registry such as ClinicalTrials.gov should minimize the risk of reporting bias. However, records may be modified during a trial and the resulting discrepancies are not always apparent without a detailed examination of all version histories, a process that is cumbersome when performed manually. We developed an automated workflow to investigate whether specific changes to RCT registry entries are associated with primary endpoint positivity. Our pipeline extracts RCT records from ClinicalTrials.gov and systematically detects changes between successive versions using a combination of deterministic textual analysis and large language model (LLM)-assisted classification. We could show a positive association between trial positivity and changes to primary outcomes (OR 1.91; 95% CI 1.48-2.47) as well as to arms and interventions (OR 2.10; 95% CI 1.62-2.73). Associations were weaker when changes occurred exclusively before the primary completion date, pointing to the importance of timing in evaluating potentially consequential modifications to RCT design. Our automated pipeline can enable analysis of trial registration records at scale, facilitating the work of reviewers and meta-scientists to promote research integrity.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Deep Learning Approaches in Genome-Wide Association Studies.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have been instrumental in uncovering the genetic basis of complex traits, yet classical single-variant testing remains limited in power and biological interpretability. Over the past decade, GWAS methodology has expanded from purely statistical association frameworks toward integrative models that incorporate functional annotations, multi-trait information, and data-driven prioritization strategies. Early developments leveraged regulatory genomics and cross-phenotype statistics to improve locus discovery, while machine learning approaches enabled systematic ranking of sub-threshold variants. More recently, deep learning architectures, including Transformer-based frameworks, have been introduced to integrate GWAS summary signals with linkage disequilibrium patterns and diverse genomic annotations. In parallel, multi-omics integration and transfer learning across related traits have emerged as practical solutions for limited sample sizes and population heterogeneity. This chapter reviews the evolving methodological landscape of AI-enabled GWAS, highlights key advances in variant discovery and functional interpretation, and discusses remaining challenges such as ancestry bias, interpretability, and the need for biological validation. Together, these approaches provide a foundation for more context-aware and scalable genetic studies of complex disease.

title: OpenTME: An Open Dataset of AI-powered H&E Tumor Microenvironment Profiles from TCGA
desc: The tumor microenvironment (TME) plays a central role in cancer progression, treatment response, and patient outcomes, yet large-scale, consistent, and quantitative TME characterization from routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained histopathology remains scarce. We introduce OpenTME, an open-access dataset of pre-computed TME profiles derived from 5,268 H&E-stained whole-slide images across ten cancer types (bladder, breast, colorectal, head and neck, liver, lung, ovarian, pancreatic, prostate, and stomach cancer) from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA). All outputs were generated using HETA (H&E Tissue Analysis), an AI-powered application built on the Atlas family of pathology foundation models, which performs tissue quality control, tissue segmentation, cell detection and classification, tumor zone and tertiary lymphoid structure (TLS) detection, and spatial neighborhood analysis, yield

title: WakeSentry: real-time awakening detection from single-channel EEG across sleep cohorts and forehead headbands
desc: Objective/Background: Awakenings after sleep onset are a core measure of sleep continuity, and EEG headbands and closed-loop stimulators, now used at home, must detect each one as it happens, to count it or to stop stimulation. Open sleep stagers match expert scorers, yet have been evaluated only offline over whole nights, so their real-time performance is untested. Patients/Methods: To fill this gap, we developed WakeSentry, which reads only past frontal EEG and learns the moment of waking through an awakening module. We tested it on 1,529 nights from five polysomnography (PSG) cohorts, three clinical, each held out of training, and on 224 headband nights, against GSSC, U-Sleep and YASA. Results: At a matched rate of 0.5 false awakenings per hour, WakeSentry caught more awakenings than GSSC in every cohort and on both headbands. On PSG its sensitivity rose from 63.8% to 70.5%, above U-Sleep and YASA on average. On the headbands it rose from 49.8% to 53.9%, a gain lost without the awakening module. With thresholds preset on the training cohorts, it still outperformed GSSC in six of seven test sets, with at most 0.40 false awakenings per hour. As a replayed stimulator gate, it shortened stimulation during wake in five test sets while staying open for at least 85% of N2 and N3. Conclusions: WakeSentry therefore works in patients and on unseen headbands. It can count awakenings at home and stop stimulation at each one, enabling multi-night monitoring of insomnia and closed-loop stimulation that stops when the sleeper wakes.

title: Advanced Flexible Wearables for Next-Generation Digital Healthcare.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] The growing emphasis on personalized medicine is accelerating the shift toward precision healthcare, demanding real-time, high-frequency physiological data acquisition through minimally invasive or noninvasive means. Flexible wearable electronics have emerged as a transformative solution, overcoming the limitations of conventional rigid medical devices. By integrating highly compliant materials with miniaturized systems, these platforms enable continuous, stable, and comfortable monitoring of multimodal physiological signals such as electrocardiograms (ECG), body temperature, blood pressure, and sweat biomarkers. This chapter explores cutting-edge advances in flexible wearable technology, such as electronic skin with sweat management, implantable bioresorbable microneedles (IBMN), self-powered haptic interfaces, and deep learning-enhanced biosignal processing. We analyze the role of these innovations in advancing intelligent, patient-centric digital healthcare while addressing challenges in clinical translation and scalability.

title: RadMatch: Auditable Radiology Report Evaluation via Finding-Level Matching
desc: As AI systems are increasingly used to draft radiology reports, reliably evaluating their clinical quality remains a critical challenge. We introduce RadMatch, a multi-stage LLM-based framework that turns report evaluation into a structured, auditable finding-level record. It extracts findings from a reference and a candidate report, matches them by clinical equivalence, grades each match over ten clinical attributes, and gives every match and unmatched finding a verdict and a clinical-significance tier. To validate metrics on CT, we build and release MetricEval-BodyCT, the first public metric-evaluation benchmark of chest and abdomen CT reports annotated by radiologists error by error. title: The Shrinking Grace Period and the Downsizing of Ransomware Victims: Exploitation Timelines and Breach Size Among US Health Care Providers, 2016-2026
desc: Objectives: To examine how quickly software vulnerabilities are exploited after public disclosure, and whether hacking breaches at US health care providers changed in size after 2021, a period in which earlier studies had found attacks concentrating on large organizations. Methods: Retrospective analysis of public data. We linked the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (1,748 entries) with CVE publication dates to measure time to confirmed exploitation by half-year of publication (2021-2025). We also analyzed 8,029 breach reports submitted to the HHS Office for Civil Rights, focusing on hacking/IT incidents at health care providers. Results: Median time to confirmed exploitation was 24 days for vulnerabilities published from late 2021 to mid 2022, 0 days for those published in the second half of 2022, and 6 days in 2023-2025, with no further shortening across 2023-2025 (P = .40). About a quarter were exploited on or before the day of disclosure. Among provider hacking breaches, the share affecting fewer than 5,000 people fell from 42% in 2016 to 32% in 2022 (trend P = .004) and rose to 46% in 2025 (P < .001). Conclusions: The window between disclosure and exploitation had narrowed to about a week before generative AI was widely available. After 2022, breaches moved toward smaller events, reversing the earlier concentration on large organizations. Defenses that depend on patching speed will not protect small providers.

title: Precision immunopharmacology in xenotransplantation: integrating genome-engineered donors, organoid testbeds, and AI-guided translation.
desc: [International immunopharmacology] Xenotransplantation is moving from isolated proof-of-concept procedures toward an engineered biotechnology platform for organ replacement. This review examines how genome-designed donor pigs, recipient-directed immunopharmacology, human-relevant in vitro testbeds, and data-driven decision systems can be integrated to address the remaining barriers to clinical translation. CRISPR-Cas-based engineering enables deletion of dominant carbohydrate xenoantigens, insertion of human complement- and coagulation-regulatory genes, modulation of innate and adaptive immune checkpoints, control of donor-organ growth, and inactivation of porcine endogenous retrovirus sequences. However, donor engineering does not eliminate residual T-cell, B-cell, antibody, complement, natural killer (NK) cell, macrophage, and inflammatory responses. Contemporary immunopharmacological strategies therefore increasingly combine costimulation blockade with complement inhibition, lymphocyte-directed therapy, and selected cytokine- or innate-immune interventions, with future regimens requiring closer integration of pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic monitoring with donor genotype and organ-specific risk. Organoids and microfluidic vascular systems may provide an intermediate testing layer by quantifying antibody binding, complement activation, endothelial injury, coagulation, leukocyte transmigration, cytokine responses, and tissue-specific function under controlled conditions before escalation to large-animal studies. Artificial intelligence may further support xenoantigen discovery, genome-editing design, donor-recipient matching, multimodal rejection surveillance, and ultimately clinician-supervised immunopharmacological decision support. We propose that these components should be connected through a traceable design-build-test-learn workflow linking computational prediction, donor construction, standardized functional testing, non-human-primate validation, and early human data. Durable translation will depend not on any single technological advance, but on reproducible donor manufacturing, precision immune control, validated human-relevant test systems, standardized longitudinal data, pathogen surveillance, organ-specific management, and transparent regulatory governance.

title: Ischemic Stroke Segmentation and Net Water Uptake Quantification on Multicenter Non-Contrast CT Using Supervised Target-Domain Adaptation
desc: Quantitative assessment of infarct hypodensity on non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT), including net water uptake (NWU), requires manual or semi-manual lesion delineation, often guided by CT perfusion or diffusion-weighted MRI, limiting clinical applicability. Automated NCCT segmentation could enable such biomarker extraction but remains challenging across heterogeneous multicenter data. This study developed and externally tested a deep learning framework for ischemic stroke segmentation and NWU quantification on NCCT. title: Deep Learning for Protein-Compound Interaction Prediction: Methods and Generalization.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] Deep learning now underpins most protein-compound interaction (PCI) prediction pipelines, spanning virtual screening, affinity estimation, and lead optimization. Yet strong numbers on standard benchmarks do not reliably translate into discovery outcomes: accuracy can drop sharply under distribution shift, many predictions are hard to rationalize or corroborate with physical evidence, and reported performance is often sensitive to how labels are defined, how data are split, and which metrics are emphasized. In this review, we introduce recent progress in deep learning for PCI prediction across task definitions, protein/ligand representations, interaction modeling architectures, benchmark resources, and evaluation practice, emphasizing the methodological choices that determine reliability outside curated test sets. We relate widely used label and task setups to their underlying assumptions and typical failure modes, analyze how redundancy and similarity leakage can inflate in-distribution results, and highlight recurring trade-offs between model expressiveness, scalability, physical realism, and generalization to unseen targets or chemotypes. We end by outlining practical priorities for evaluation and reporting, including split protocols matched to the intended deployment scenario, explicit treatment of assay heterogeneity, uncertainty-aware and decision-focused metrics, and benchmark designs that better anticipate prospective utility.

title: Mammography Foundation Models for Opportunistic Prediction of Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events
desc: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death among women, yet cardiovascular risk assessment often relies on clinical variables that may be missing, outdated, or unavailable in routine care. Screening mammography offers an opportunity for opportunistic cardiovascular risk stratification because it is routinely acquired and contains vascular features, including breast arterial calcifications (BAC), that are associated with cardiovascular risk and events. We evaluate whether mammography specific foundation models, originally pretrained for breast cancer related tasks, can transfer to cardiovascular risk prediction without cardiovascular specific supervision or explicit BAC annotation. title: MedExAgent: Training LLM Agents to Ask, Examine, and Diagnose in Noisy Clinical Environments
desc: Real-world clinical diagnosis is a complex process in which the doctor is required to obtain information from both interaction with the patient and conducting medical exams. Additionally, the doctor needs to adapt to different patient personas, as well as noisy and incomplete information that can happen at any time during the process. However, existing benchmarks for medical LLMs and methods for automatic diagnosis largely simplify this process by reducing it to single-turn question answering, noise-free conversations, or sequential exam making, etc., ignoring the interactive and uncertain nature of clinical diagnosis. desc: Hospital quality improvement (QI) programs generally proceed in two stages: (1) hypothesis generation, which identifies candidate factors that may improve care quality and efficiency, and (2) confirmatory analyses, which implement and evaluate QI initiatives targeting these factors. Although most research focuses on the confirmatory stage, hypothesis generation is equally important because it shapes where teams focus their effort. Currently, hypothesis generation depends on expert-driven, qualitative methods (e.g., Lean Healthcare tools) that can be anecdotal, hard to reproduce, time-consuming, and resource-intensive. desc: Efforts to keep clinical language models safe have concentrated on what enters and leaves the model, but a manipulated model can return an answer that looks entirely ordinary. desc: The curation of large cohort datasets for developing deep learning models demands annotating or editing over the AI-predicted labels. However, openly available annotation tools are time-consuming, as they involve complex navigational steps and do not support batch processing. This study aimed to develop a simple, fast, semiautomated batch-annotation tool named MedImgAnnotator. The tool was created by integrating editing tools, image mask pair matching logic, preprocessing functions, object detection tool, and a plugin management system. Its performance was evaluated in terms of active annotation time and ease of use by the developer and 12 users using open-source MR and CT scans. desc: Surgical resection remains the only potentially curative treatment for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), and eligibility depends on accurate assessment of vascular invasion (VI), i.e., tumor extension into adjacent critical vessels. Despite its importance for preoperative staging and surgical planning, computational VI assessment remains underexplored. Two major challenges are the lack of public datasets and the diagnostic ambiguity at the tumor-vessel interface, which leads to substantial inter-rater variability even among expert radiologists. To address these limitations, we introduce the CURVAS-PDACVI Dataset and Challenge, an open benchmark for uncertainty-aware AI in PDAC staging based on a densely annotated dataset with five independent expert annotations per scan. title: How Well Do Segmentation Foundation Models Generalize Across Structural and Functional Medical Imaging?
desc: Segmentation foundation models offer reusable tools for universal medical-image segmentation, but their development and evaluation have largely centered on structural CT and MRI imaging. Functional imaging such as PET provides complementary metabolic information yet remains less studied and validated. Moreover, existing evaluations often involve different datasets and tasks, making modality-associated variation difficult to distinguish from differences in segmentation targets and data distributions. To enable a more direct comparison, we introduce UMD, a whole-body multi-organ dataset comprising 490 PET/CT and 464 PET/MRI examinations with 13 annotated organs (approximately 675,000 2D slices and 12,000 3D organ annotations). title: Why ML-based cough models do not generalize: a systematic cross-dataset evaluation for tuberculosis screening
desc: Cough acoustics are promising for non-invasive tuberculosis (TB) screening, yet whether machine learning (ML) models capture disease-related acoustics or artifacts of data collection remains unresolved. We evaluated the cross-dataset generalizability of classical ML and deep learning (DL) cough-based TB classifiers across three independent datasets. Despite moderate within-dataset performance (ROC-AUC up to $0.76 \pm 0.06$), both pipelines fail to generalize, with external performance frequently below 0.6, indicating a possible limitation of the data. desc: While test-time scaling enhances Large Language Model (LLM) agents in long-horizon software engineering (SWE), sparse binary rewards (Pass/Fail) create a severe credit assignment crisis and waste failed exploratory trajectories. desc: The ability to shape health behaviors of large populations automatically, across wearable types and disease conditions at scale has tremendous potential to improve global health outcomes. title: Tracking Representations in LLM Reasoning Traces for Iterated Games
desc: Large language model (LLM) agents achieve state-of-the-art performance across domains through chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning. Despite their ubiquitous use, little is understood about the relationship between the externalized trace and the model's actual computation. We address this by investigating how LLM agents make decisions in iterative games with incomplete information. Using a series of mechanistic interpretability techniques, we find that the model forms and iteratively revises an internal representation of the game throughout the CoT. Once the model prematurely commits to an incorrect belief, it rarely recovers. This failure is manifested in both the literal trace and the layer activations. desc: Agent-based AI has enabled the automation of tasks by exposing application tools and resources to large language models (LLMs). However, to improve scope and accuracy, agents are often given access rights that exceed those of ordinary users, introducing significant security risks and potential regulatory breaches. This paper applies the AI Trust, Risk, and Security Management (TRiSM) framework to a medical report-generation application to demonstrate how an insecure baseline workflow can be transformed into a security-conscious agentic workflow. desc: Background: Precision oncology requires integration of heterogeneous molecular and pathology data, yet many fusion models offer limited biologically grounded interpretability and struggle with missing modalities. desc: Barrett's esophagus dysplasia grading suffers substantial inter-observer variability, particularly for low-grade dysplasia, complicating clinical decision-making. title: A Subspecialty Diagnostic System Powered by Self-Supervised Learning for Cervical Histopathology
desc: Cervical cancer remains a major malignancy in women, with large-scale human papillomavirus-based screening generating a large volume of biopsies and, for advanced cases, surgical specimens, imposing an overwhelming diagnostic burden that necessitates precise histopathological evaluation. Although deep learning shows promise, general foundation models offer a broader reach but remain limited in capturing subspecialty-specific features and task adaptability. desc: A unified 3D medical foundation model promises reusable, frozen features that serve a wide variety of tasks such as segmentation, classification and registration on MRI, CT and PET as well as specialist models do. desc: To develop and evaluate an uncertainty-aware multimodal learning framework for predicting radiation-induced xerostomia in patients receiving head-and-neck cancer radiotherapy. title: QUTCC: Quantile Uncertainty Training and Conformal Calibration for Imaging Inverse Problems
desc: While deep learning offers tremendous promise for scientific and medical imaging, any failures and hallucinations (predictions that do not coincide with reality) are hard to pinpoint and can have serious downstream consequences. desc: The rapid scale-up of AI infrastructure has made datacenter reliability a cornerstone of the cloud business economy. desc: Anomaly detection in medical images is a complex task, requiring the development of a robust model using only healthy patient data. desc: AI-generated bug reports have drawn criticism for unreliable claims and faulty reproducers that burden maintainers. desc: Clinical large language models are usually judged by whether the final answer is right. desc: Structure-preserving de-identification replaces protected health information (PHI) with realistic same-type surrogates ("Anna S." becomes "Maria S.", not [NAME]). desc: Generalist CT foundation models detect many findings with high performance, but their ability to differentiate detected lesions remains largely unevaluated. desc: High-quality causal reasoning datasets are essential for developing models with reliable causal understanding, particularly in specialized domains. desc: The electric power sector is a leading source of air pollutant emissions, impacting the public health of nearly every community. desc: Medical vision--language models (VLMs) often need to identify small, subtle lesions within high-resolution images containing extensive normal anatomy and redundant visual information. desc: Acquiring every feature of an instance is often costly: a measurement can carry a monetary price, a time delay, or a privacy cost. desc: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) remains a leading cause of vision loss among working-age adults worldwide, making reliable severity grading clinically important. desc: X-ray is widely applied for transmission imaging due to its stronger penetration than natural light. desc: Coronary angiography (CAG) is the gold-standard imaging modality for evaluating coronary artery disease, but its interpretation and subsequent treatment planning rely heavily on expert cardiologists. desc: Biomedical entity linking maps textual mentions to concepts in structured knowledge bases such as UMLS or SNOMED CT. desc: Integrating IoT devices into household systems offers enhanced control over living environments. desc: Strong models in algorithmic statistics are essentially the cells of simple partitions of $\{0,1\}^n$. desc: Pretraining filtering is one of the most common safeguards for open-weight language models. title: SurgCBVR: A Multi-Domain Benchmark for Content-Based Surgical Video-to-Video Retrieval
desc: Hospitals record thousands of hours of surgical video annually, yet these archives remain difficult to search by content. desc: While multimodal language models can interpret diagrams and generate structured outputs, their capacity to connect passive radio-frequency (RF) design intent, layout geometry, and electromagnetic behavior remains largely untested. desc: Accurate outdoor positioning in cellular networks is hindered by sparse, heterogeneous measurement collections and the high cost of exhaustive site surveys. desc: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) improves Large Language Models (LLMs) by grounding generation in external, non-parametric knowledge. desc: Generative models and autonomous agents now propose candidate inorganic crystals by the million, yet most screens test little beyond a minimum-distance cutoff and give no chemical reason for failure. desc: Laws are increasingly turned into programs that decide cases, such as whether a firm was a small or medium enterprise (SME) on a given date, and large language models (LLMs) now write them. desc: Reconstructing cellular dynamics from snapshots is challenging because the destructive nature of single-cell measurements makes tracking the same cells over time impossible. Growth-based methods represent population change as a rate on the density, which does not assign exits and entries to individual cells. Unbalanced Schrödinger bridges model individual events, but neural solvers for killed diffusion bridges simulate trajectories during training. We introduce Elysium, a simulation-free solver that jointly learns state transition and mass change. Using a killed Brownian reference and its time reversal, Elysium constructs direct regression objectives from an optimal endpoint coupling and conditional bridge distributions, without simulating trajectories during training.

desc: Inverse RNA Folding consists of finding a nucleotide sequence that folds into a predefined secondary structure. It is useful for synthetic biology, medicine, and nanotechnology. title: How to "train" a surgeon? Benchmarking generalist agents in surgical scene understanding
desc: Evaluating general-purpose multimodal large language models (MLLMs) for surgical scene understanding remains limited due to scarce surgical data and fragmented evaluation protocols. We address these challenges through a two-stage evaluation framework for surgical scene understanding. title: Controllable Chains of Thought Can Reveal Less, Even Without Evasion Training
desc: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring is a promising tool for detecting hidden goals, off-task behavior, and other failures in AI agents. title: AIstatLab at BraTS-GoAT 2026 Task 3: Quality-Controlled Consensus Pseudo-Labeling and Dense Expert Adaptation
desc: BraTS-GoAT Task 3 evaluates brain-tumor segmentation across heterogeneous entities using shared ET, TC, and WT regions. desc: Medical-image embeddings are increasingly shared in place of raw images for authorized downstream tasks, yet they may reveal sensitive attributes. desc: Medical vision-language agents increasingly rely on segmentation tools, and recent work has focused on acquiring the right mask, often treating a good mask as the end point of tool use. But do these agents use the resulting evidence effectively? desc: Generative engines synthesize retrieved web pages into answers, recommendations, and rankings. Generative engine optimization (GEO) services sell visibility in these answers by publishing promotional articles on user-generated-content (UGC) platforms for paying clients. Such promotion raises concerns in medical and financial domains, where misleading advice can cause harm. desc: Representing videos on uniform spatio-temporal grids produces large token sequences and substantial computational costs. desc: While text-to-image (T2I) diffusion models achieve remarkable quality, they risk producing harmful content. desc: Harmful algal blooms threaten water quality and public health, yet automated segmentation of bloom regions in freshwater imagery is limited by scarce pixel-level annotations. desc: Paired image restoration spans changes in imaging contrast, sensor modality, and spatial resolution. We present the Unified Residual Translator (URT), which separates fixed channel and scale mapping from learned residual prediction. title: Structure-Aware Sparse-View X-ray 3D Reconstruction
desc: X-ray, known for its ability to reveal internal structures of objects, is expected to provide richer information for 3D reconstruction than visible light. desc: A cell observed after a gene knockdown has an uncertain future, both in how its appearance will evolve and when it will divide. desc: The ultimate ambition of visual quality assessment is to reproduce the neural computations of human vision and thereby achieve full alignment with human perception. desc: Multi-source audio-to-image generation exhibits consistent compositional failures when audio tokens occupy geometrically displaced, semantically unanchored positions in the CLIP text-token space, where the diffusion U-Net lacks the prior to reliably attend to them or ground them in distinct spatial regions. desc: Small lesions in brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are easily missed: a segmentation model can reach a high Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) while leaving many of them undetected. desc: We propose NullFlow, a principled framework for one-step generative image reconstruction. Our key idea is to confine the generative flow to a measurement-consistent subspace. desc: Although vision foundation models (VFMs) are increasingly reused for biomedical image analysis, it remains unclear whether the latent representations they provide are general enough to support effective transfer and reuse across heterogeneous microscopy image datasets. desc: Self-verification is increasingly used to improve the reliability of vision-language models (VLMs) and provide feedback for iterative self-correction, yet it is useful only when checking an answer provides information that discriminates correct from incorrect predictions rather than simply re-solving the same visual problem. desc: Generative inpainting of brain MRI volumes is essential for synthesizing healthy tissue in pathological regions, improving the accuracy and reliability of automated downstream brain analysis applications such as image registration, brain extraction, and segmentation. desc: The ability to generate multimodal reports integrating fluent narratives with faithful visualizations from tabular data, has become a cornerstone capability for modern vision-language models in practical domains such as finance, healthcare, and policy making. desc: Automated hate speech detection degrades over time as everyday vocabulary is weaponized into covert slurs while retaining original benign meanings (polysemy retention).
